insights.headline: Gold posts biggest weekly drop since June as yields top 5%; India's festive demand holds firm
insights.summary: Comex gold fell 3.59% to $4,133.70 this week — the largest weekly decline since early June and the lowest settlement since August — while silver slid 6.68% below $60. A weak US jobs report briefly lifted bullion before 10-year Treasury yields above 5% and a firm dollar pulled it back, leaving Wall Street bearish. In India, gold is about 7% cheaper than August near ₹1.5 lakh per 10 grams, and festive demand is holding ahead of Dhanteras even as August imports slumped 58%. Central banks keep buying, underpinning the $4,000 floor.
points: Comex gold -3.59% to $4,133.70, biggest weekly fall since June; silver -6.68% to $59.977, lowest since August.
US added 29k jobs vs ~90k expected; October Fed-hike odds fell, but 10-year yields held above 5%.
India: gold ~₹1.5 lakh/10g with MCX facing resistance; buyers shift to silver; an MCX silver option spiked ₹174 to ₹2,300 in minutes.
Dhanteras demand steady despite high prices; August gold imports fell 58% YoY; festive buying tilts to lighter jewellery.
RBI's forex reserves fell a record $18.34bn to $747.56bn as rupee pressure mounted.

trending.title: Yields are running the show
trending.summary: Every gold move this week traces back to the bond market: weak payrolls briefly lifted bullion, then 10-year yields above 5% and a firm dollar dragged it to the biggest weekly loss since June.

trending.title: India's Dhanteras test
trending.summary: Gold is 7% cheaper than August near ₹1.5 lakh, and demand is holding — buyers adjust to lighter pieces and silver while imports slump 58% ahead of November 6.

trending.title: Silver's two stories
trending.summary: In India, silver demand was waiting on import licences, not missing. Globally, silver just posted its worst week since June, sliding below $60 as Deutsche Bank flags oversupply.

trending.title: Central banks keep stacking
trending.summary: South Korea will buy gold from producers in December; China and Poland added to reserves in August. Official-sector buying is the floor under gold near $4,000.

items.title: Wall Street on the brink of bearish majority after gold's post-payrolls slide
items.summary: Kitco's weekly gold survey after Friday's slide shows Wall Street teetering on a bearish majority while Main Street abandoned the bullish bias it had held since July, after gold failed to hold above $4,200 and finished the week near session lows. Bannockburn's Marc Chandler likes gold higher next week on weak jobs and Fed patience; Adrian Day expects it lower; Adam Button stays neutral.

items.title: Comex Gold Ends the Week 3.59% Lower at $4133.70
items.summary: Comex gold for October delivery lost $154.10, or 3.59%, to $4,133.70 this week — the largest one-week decline since early June, the second straight weekly loss, and the lowest settlement since August 4. Silver fared worse, down 6.68% to $59.977, its lowest settlement since August 3. Year-to-date, gold is down 4.44% and silver 14.48%, per Dow Jones Market Data.

items.title: Gold eases 7% before Dhanteras as imports slump 58% and buyers shift to digital gold
items.summary: India's gold price has cooled about 7% from its August peak to roughly ₹1.48 lakh per 10g (IBJA, Oct 1), with the trade guarded ahead of Dhanteras on November 6. August gold imports fell 58% year on year to $2.3 billion under the 15% import duty, while Indian gold ETFs drew ₹25.97 billion of fresh money in August and dealers widened discounts to about $78 an ounce, a sign of soft physical demand.

items.title: Gold at Rs 1.5 lakh per 10 grams is pushing middle-class Indian buyers to silver
items.summary: Indian buyers are shifting from gold to silver this festive season: 10g of 24-karat gold costs about Rs 1.5 lakh — the same money buys roughly 650g of silver, TOI reports. The IBJA estimates Diwali-season silver demand will rise 17-18% year-on-year; silver imports topped $1 billion in August, up 127% on the year. A Surat jeweller says silver now makes up to 35% of yearly revenue, up from 10%.

items.title: MCX Gold Faces Rs 1.5 Lakh Resistance After Yield Spike
items.summary: MCX gold October futures jumped 1.02% to Rs 1,47,649/10g but face a Rs 1.5 lakh resistance after a US Treasury yield spike, NDTV Profit reports, while MCX silver December futures rose 0.94% to Rs 2,25,804/kg. The article lists the key support and resistance levels traders are watching on both metals.

items.title: Cyber manipulation in commodity market: Silver option price jumped from ₹174 to ₹2,300 in 5 minutes
items.summary: Cybercriminals breached a Noida risk-management firm's servers and used its static IP to place 1,238 unauthorized orders across 5,559 illiquid MCX silver option contracts. The contract spiked from ₹174 to ₹2,300 in five minutes; about ₹12 crore in premiums created false liquidity while counterparties siphoned roughly ₹11 crore. CERT-In confirmed deliberate distortion; one arrest made.

items.title: US yields rise, reversing initial reaction to weak jobs report
items.summary: US Treasury yields reversed an early decline after the weak September jobs report, the 10-year climbing 4.72 bps to 5.281% as traders priced ~80% odds of a Fed hold this month. Gold futures erased their payrolls pop — up 1.4% to $4,259, then down 1.2% to $4,153.80, the biggest blown gain in almost a month, per Dow Jones Market Data.

items.title: Fed officials give hints on rate decision as markets cut October rate hike odds
items.summary: Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson and New York Fed President John Williams signaled the central bank can take its time before another rate increase. Markets repriced sharply: October hike odds fell from about 70% to 25% on federal funds futures, and Goldman Sachs economists said an October hike is unlikely. Chicago Fed's Austan Goolsbee kept both a hike and a cut on the table.

items.title: Gold's resilience supports strong outlook, silver faces oversupply, copper could be the big gainer – Deutsche Bank's Ghali
items.summary: Deutsche Bank's Ghali said gold's pullback has been 'incredibly limited' despite 10-year yields above 5% and oil over $100, with positioning most bearish since October 2021 while official buying runs at double the 2022 pace. Silver has tipped into oversupply - London inventories highest since November 2024, solar demand down a third - and should lag gold; copper holds the biggest potential gains.

items.title: Soft September jobs report sends markets higher
items.summary: US employers added just 29,000 jobs in September, far below the 90,000 economists expected, while the unemployment rate ticked up to 4.2%. Treasury yields fell and the odds of a Fed rate hike at the October meeting dropped to around 12-19%. Gold rose 0.8% to $4,210 on the cooler data.

items.title: Bank of Korea plans gold purchase from domestic producers in December
items.summary: South Korea's central bank plans to buy gold from domestic producers in December - its first reserve addition since 2013. The transaction system should be ready by December 14, when about 1 tonne could be available; the bank announced the resumption in August and bought $250 million of gold ETFs in Q2. The BOK holds 104.4 tonnes, about 3% of reserves, all stored in London.

items.title: China, Poland’s Central Bank Gold Buying Spree Creates a $4K Price Floor
items.summary: Gold fell roughly 6% in September to a seven-week low near $4,110–$4,150 as 10-year Treasury yields near 5.3%, hawkish Fed rhetoric and a strong dollar raised the cost of holding bullion. The longer-term floor comes from central-bank accumulation led by China and Poland diversifying away from fiat, with desks such as Morgan Stanley viewing $4,000 as major psychological and technical support.

items.title: Silver Prices Fall ₹5,000 Today, Down ₹10,000 This Week
items.summary: Delhi bullion trade saw gold add ₹500 on Thursday to ₹1,49,800 per 10 grams on a weaker rupee — ₹96.31 against the dollar, its softest in over two months — even as silver fell ₹5,000 to ₹2.27 lakh per kg. For the week, gold is down about ₹2,800 and silver about ₹10,000. Bullion markets are closed today for Gandhi Jayanti.

items.title: Silver price forecast: bears crowd $60 after six-percent weekly rout
items.summary: Silver retreated about 0.76% on Friday to $60.50 as Treasury yields edged higher and capped the dollar's payroll-driven dip, FXStreet reports. The white metal finished the week with losses of over 6%, trading below the 50- and 100-day SMAs at $64.06-$64.74 and poised to test $60; RSI stays below 50. Support sits at $60, then the August low of $56.57, with the year-to-date low of $54.77 below that.

items.title: Silver's India Problem Was Policy, Not Demand
items.summary: India's silver imports fell to 46.8 tonnes in May from 534.3 tonnes a year earlier after the duty rose to 15% and licence rules tightened, recovering to about 15.5 million ounces in August as permits arrived, per Heraeus. MCX silver stood 17% above the world price on September 30, and demand from jewellery, coins, ETFs and industry stays intact, the analysis says. Silver was collateral damage...

items.title: India's Forex Reserves Plunge by $18.34 Billion
items.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves fell $18.34 billion to $747.56 billion in the week ended September 25, RBI data released on Friday showed — the third straight weekly decline, pulling the kitty further from its September 4 record of $785.71 billion. Foreign currency assets dropped $15.57 billion to $615.41 billion as the RBI sold dollars to steady the rupee, while gold reserves fell $2.59...

items.title: Gold Demand Remains Strong Despite High Prices, Buyers Adjust Purchases
items.summary: The World Gold Council expects Indian gold demand to improve through the festive and wedding season on steady investment demand and resilient wedding buying despite near-record prices. With 24-carat gold around ₹1.48 lakh per 10 grams, Guwahati jewellers expect robust but smaller purchases — lighter jewellery, coins or digital gold — while old-gold exchange has widened domestic discounts.

items.title: Gold gets its festive shine back as lower prices lure Asian buyers
items.summary: Lower gold prices are pulling physical buyers back across Asia ahead of the festive season, the Times of India reports: Indian dealer discounts narrowed from up to $43/oz to $14/oz as demand improved, Singapore dealers saw stronger buying as they rebuilt inventories, and China is watching price moves closely with premiums running high.

items.title: Gold (XAUUSD), Silver, Platinum Forecasts – Gold Retreats As Treasury Yields Rebound
items.summary: Gold slid back below $4,160 after failing to hold $4,200, as 10-year Treasury yields climbed toward 5.30% despite the weak September payrolls report. FXEmpire flags $4,000–$4,020 as the next support if $4,160 breaks.

items.title: '50% of silver rally was just bubble': experts pick gold and platinum
items.summary: Four Indian market experts argue about half of silver's early-2026 rally was a speculative bubble — the metal has fallen from a January peak of Rs 3.86 lakh/kg to about Rs 2.22 lakh — and they now favour gold and platinum, Bhaskar English reports. They see silver possibly recovering toward Rs 3-4 lakh/kg by 2027, though small investors may wait until end-2027 to recoup older holdings.
